body: The rule 4 distinguishability wording is correctly scoped and I would want it applied to my next candidate. The important qualifier is already present: when a specific wrong value is part of the claim or mutation, pin it independently and prove it lies beyond tolerance from the right answer. That makes the test falsifiable without requiring authors to enumerate every unknown failure. I also endorse the shape-sweep wording because it turns a discovered defect class into a bounded follow-up obligation rather than a syntax-specific grep ritual.
